# Digital-Tool @ Stage 10 — Concrete Peak

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 72 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Digital-tool at Order 8 is **framework-evaluation**: the agent can now step outside
its own tool framework and evaluate it against alternative frameworks. "User-centered
design produces intuitive interfaces but may miss systemic implications. Systems design
produces robust architectures but may miss user needs. Which tradeoff is acceptable?"
This is the post-modern tool insight: every tool design embodies values, and different
value systems produce different tool approaches.

The key advance from Stage 9 is **tool pluralism**. The agent no longer constructs tool
systems within a single framework — it evaluates multiple frameworks and recognizes that
each embodies different values.

Tool use at Stage 10 is understood as **value-laden**. The agent recognizes that
"usable" tool design is not a neutral concept — it presupposes that usability is the
right criterion, which is itself a value choice.

This framework-evaluation capacity opens up **genuine tool pluralism**. The agent can
hold multiple tool paradigms simultaneously without collapsing into relativism.

But tool reasoning at Stage 10 is still **framework-dependent**. The agent evaluates
frameworks from within a meta-framework but cannot step outside that meta-framework.

The transition from Stage 10 to Stage 11 occurs when the agent can integrate multiple
tool frameworks into a coherent meta-system.

In human development, Stage 10 corresponds to the thinker who can evaluate tool
paradigms across frameworks.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** Cultural tool pluralism becomes institutionalized.

- **UR:** The individual agent can evaluate tool paradigms from outside any particular
  framework.

- **LL:** Multi-paradigm tool institutions emerge: design studios that span paradigms,
  interdisciplinary tool research centers.

- **LR:** The design studio, the tool journal, the interdisciplinary research institute.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Paradigm paralysis — cannot commit to any tool paradigm.

- **Dark allergy:** Framework fundamentalism — insists one tool paradigm is superior.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to pluralism as an identity.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting pluralism as moral weakness.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Framework evaluation:** The agent can articulate value assumptions in tool
  paradigms.

- **Paradigm comparison:** The agent can compare tool approaches across paradigms.

- **Value-aware tool reasoning:** The agent recognizes that "usable" presupposes
  values.

- **Meta-framework dependency:** The agent evaluates from within a meta-framework but
  cannot evaluate the meta-framework.
